content: Magnesium sulfate can enhance the effects of inhaled loxapine through an unknown mechanism. It is important to exercise caution and monitor for signs of increased central nervous system (CNS) depression, especially when higher doses of magnesium sulfate are used in combination with other CNS depressants. The combination of sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate can increase the effects of lurasidone through an unknown mechanism. Close monitoring is recommended to detect any signs of enhanced CNS depression when these agents are used together. Sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate can increase the toxicity of macimorelin by prolonging the QTc interval. Patients at higher risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias should have preand post-colonoscopy electrocardiograms (ECGs) performed to monitor for potential adverse effects. The coadministration of sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate with magaldrate may increase the risk of adverse events such as seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment due to fluid and electrolyte abnormalities. Caution and close monitoring are advised. Magnesium sulfate can increase the toxicity of magnesium oxide when used together. This combination may elevate the risk of adverse events related to fluid and electrolyte imbalances, including seizures, arrhythmias, and renal dysfunction. Monitoring is essential. The combination of sodium sulfate, potassium sulfate, and magnesium sulfate with mannitol may increase toxicity. This interaction is likely due to fluid and electrolyte disturbances, which can heighten the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Caution and monitoring are recommended. Magnesium sulfate can increase the toxicity of meclofenamate, mefenamic acid, meloxicam, and other nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) by causing fluid and electrolyte imbalances. This can lead to an increased risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Close monitoring is necessary. Magnesium sulfate can increase the toxicity of methadone by prolonging the QTc interval. Patients at risk of cardiac arrhythmias should undergo ECG monitoring before and after procedures such as colonoscopy. The coadministration of magnesium sulfate with methylprednisolone, prednisone, or other corticosteroids may increase the risk of adverse events such as seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment due to fluid and electrolyte abnormalities. Caution and monitoring are advised. Magnesium sulfate can enhance the effects of CNS depressants such as molindone, olanzapine, perphenazine, and others through an unknown mechanism. Close monitoring for signs of enhanced CNS depression is recommended when these agents are used together. Magnesium sulfate can increase the toxicity of medications such as nilotinib, pimozide, and ribociclib by prolonging the QTc interval. Patients at risk of serious cardiac arrhythmias should have ECGs performed before and after procedures to monitor for potential adverse effects. Magnesium sulfate can potentiate the effects of neuromuscular blocking agents such as pancuronium, rocuronium, and succinylcholine. Caution and monitoring for signs of muscle weakness or respiratory depression are advised. Magnesium sulfate can decrease the absorption of oral medications such as moxifloxacin, norfloxacin, and penicillamine by inhibiting gastrointestinal absorption. To avoid this interaction, administer the affected medication at least 2 hours before and no less than 6 hours after magnesium sulfate. Magnesium sulfate can increase the toxicity of angiotensin-converting enzyme (ACE) inhibitors such as ramipril, quinapril, and trandolapril, as well as angiotensin receptor blockers (ARBs) like telmisartan and olmesartan. This interaction may lead to fluid and electrolyte imbalances, increasing the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Close monitoring is recommended. Magnesium sulfate can increase the toxicity of QTc-prolonging agents such as sotalol, thioridazine, and tetrabenazine. Patients at risk of cardiac arrhythmias should have ECGs performed to monitor for potential adverse effects. Magnesium sulfate can enhance the effects of antidepressants such as nortriptyline, paroxetine, and sertraline, as well as antipsychotics like risperidone and trifluoperazine, through unknown mechanisms. Close monitoring for CNS depression or seizures is recommended, particularly when using higher doses of magnesium sulfate. Magnesium sulfate can increase the toxicity of medications such as rifampin, risedronate, and sucralfate by causing fluid and electrolyte imbalances. This can lead to an increased risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Caution and monitoring are advised. Magnesium sulfate can decrease the absorption of oral iron products, trientine, and other chelating agents. To avoid this interaction, administer the affected medication at least 1 to 2 hours before or after magnesium sulfate. Magnesium sulfate can increase the toxicity of aminoglycosides such as tobramycin and streptomycin, as well as other medications like sacubitril/valsartan and sulindac, by causing fluid and electrolyte imbalances. This can heighten the risk of seizures, arrhythmias, and renal impairment. Close monitoring is essential. Magnesium sulfate can increase the toxicity of QTc-prolonging agents such as torsemide, torsade-inducing drugs, and tetrabenazine. Patients at risk of cardiac arrhythmias should have ECGs performed to monitor for potential adverse effects.
